account.definition: a record that shows increases and decreases in one item, such as cash, sales, or wages.

account holder.definition: the person or business that owns a bank account.

accountability.definition: the duty to explain and take responsibility for actions

accounting.definition: the process of recording, organising, and reporting business money matters.

accounting cycle.definition: the steps followed in recording and preparing business accounts

accounting equation.definition: the basic rule showing that assets are equal to capital plus liabilities

accounting period.definition: a fixed length of time used to measure and report a business’s performance

accounts payable.definition: money that the business owes to suppliers for goods or services received on credit

accounts receivable.definition: money that customers owe to the business after getting goods or services on credit

accrual basis accounting.definition: a method of accounting that records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, even if cash has not yet moved

accruals.definition: expenses or income recorded before the money is actually paid or received

analysis.definition: careful study of something to understand it better

asset.definition: something valuable owned by a business

assets.definition: things a business owns that have value, such as cash, furniture, or buildings.

audit.definition: an examination of financial records to check if they are correct and reliable.

authorisation.definition: official permission or approval to do something

automation.definition: the use of machines or software to do work automatically.

balance.definition: the amount left in an account after comparing the debit side and the credit side.

balance brought forward.definition: the balance brought into a new period from the previous one.

balance carried forward.definition: the closing balance of an account that is moved to the next period.

balance sheet.definition: another name for the statement of financial position.

bank account.definition: an account at a bank used to keep and manage money.

bank deposit.definition: money paid into a bank account.

bank overdraft.definition: money a bank allows a business to withdraw even when there is not enough money in the account

bank withdrawal.definition: money taken out of a bank account.

book of prime entry.definition: a book where a business records a transaction for the first time.

book-keeping.definition: the process of recording business financial transactions in an organised way

books of accounts.definition: the records a business keeps to show its financial transactions.

books of prime entry.definition: the first books where business transactions are recorded before being posted to other accounts

budgeting.definition: planning how money will be used or spent

building.definition: a permanent structure owned or used by a business.

business.definition: an activity of buying and selling goods or services to earn money

calculate.definition: to find an amount or answer by using numbers

capital.definition: the money or other resources put into a business by the owner to start or grow it

carriage inwards.definition: the cost of transporting purchased goods to the business premises.

cash book.definition: a book used to record cash received and cash paid, including bank transactions.

cash flow.definition: the movement of cash into and out of a business.

cash flow statement.definition: a financial statement that shows how cash comes into and goes out of a business

cash outflows.definition: cash going out of a business.

cash receipt voucher.definition: a document used as proof that cash has been received.

cashflow.definition: the movement of money coming into and going out of a business

cheque.definition: a written order telling a bank to pay money from one account to another person or business

chronological order.definition: the arrangement of events in the order in which they happened.

chronologically.definition: in the order in which events or transactions happen over time.

civilisation.definition: a developed human society with its own culture and systems

closing inventory.definition: the stock of goods a business has at the end of an accounting period.

commission received.definition: money earned for selling goods or services on behalf of another person or business.

competency.definition: an important skill or ability to do something well

compliance.definition: acting according to rules or laws.

computation.definition: a calculation done to find totals, balances, or other figures

concept.definition: a basic general idea about something

consistency principle.definition: the rule that the same accounting methods should be used over time unless there is a good reason to change them

consumables.definition: items that are used up in daily business work, like soap, creams, or towels

cost.definition: the amount of money needed to buy, make, or do something

cost of goods available for sale.word: cost of goods available for sale
cost of goods available for sale.definition: the total cost of opening inventory plus net purchases that are ready to be sold.
variations: cost of goods available for sale

cost of goods sold.definition: the total cost of the goods that a business has sold during a period.

credit.definition: a way of buying or selling now and paying later.

credit balance.definition: an amount recorded on the credit side of an account.

credit entry.definition: an entry on the right side of an account, used in recording increases or decreases in certain accounts

credit note.definition: a document showing that the seller has reduced the amount a buyer owes, usually because goods were returned.

credit purchase.definition: buying goods now and paying for them later

credit sale.definition: selling goods now and receiving payment later.

creditor.definition: a person or business that is owed money by the business

current asset.definition: an asset that is expected to be turned into cash within one year or one accounting period

current liability.definition: a debt that must be paid within one year or one accounting period

customer.definition: a person or business that buys goods or services

daybook.definition: a book of original entry where business transactions are first written down.

debit.definition: an entry made on one side of an account to record part of a transaction

debit balance.definition: an amount recorded on the debit side of an account.

debit note.definition: a document sent to show that the supplier’s account has been charged because goods were returned

debtor.definition: a person or business that owes money to the business

depositor.definition: a person who puts money into a bank or a business account

depreciation.definition: the gradual reduction in the value of a long-term asset over time

discipline.definition: a subject or field of study

discount.definition: a reduction in the usual price of something

discount allowed.definition: a reduction in price given by a business to its customers.

discount received.definition: a reduction in the amount a business has to pay, often for paying early

double entry.definition: an accounting system where every transaction affects at least two accounts.

double entry principle.definition: the accounting rule that every transaction affects at least two accounts with equal debit and credit entries

double entry system.definition: an accounting system where every transaction affects at least two accounts

double-entry.definition: an accounting system where every transaction affects at least two accounts, with equal debit and credit entries.

double-entry system.definition: a bookkeeping system where every transaction is recorded in at least two accounts

drawee.definition: the bank that is ordered to pay money on a cheque.

drawer.definition: the person who writes and signs a cheque.

drawings.definition: money or assets taken out of the business by the owner for personal use

duality principle.definition: the rule that every business transaction has two equal effects in the accounts

enterprise.definition: a business or organisation that carries out commercial activities

entry.definition: a record written in the books of accounts

equipment.definition: tools or machines needed to do a job or run a business

equity.definition: the owner’s share in the business after deducting liabilities from assets

error.definition: a mistake made when recording, calculating, or posting accounting information

evaluate.definition: to examine something carefully in order to judge its value or success

evaluation.definition: the process of checking or judging how well something has been done.

expense.definition: money spent by a business in order to operate or buy goods.

expenses.definition: costs a business pays while operating, such as wages, rent, or advertising.

financial.definition: related to money and how it is managed

financial position.definition: the state of a business in terms of what it owns, what it owes, and the owner’s interest

financial statement.definition: a report that shows the financial position and performance of a business

financial statements.definition: reports that show the financial performance and position of a business.

financing activities.definition: activities related to getting or repaying money from owners or lenders.

fittings.definition: fixed items used in a building or business, such as shelves or lights

fixtures.definition: items fixed to a property, such as lights or built-in shelves

folio.definition: a reference number used to help find related entries in books of account.

furniture.definition: items such as tables, chairs, and desks used in a business

general journal.definition: the main book where business transactions are first recorded in order

general ledger.definition: the main ledger that contains all the main accounts of a business.

going concern.definition: the idea that a business will continue operating for the foreseeable future

going concern principle.definition: the idea that a business is expected to continue operating for the foreseeable future

goods.definition: things that are made or bought to be sold

gross loss.definition: the amount by which the cost of goods sold is more than net sales.

gross profit.definition: the profit made after subtracting the cost of goods sold from sales

historical cost.definition: the original price paid for an asset when the business bought it

historical cost principle.definition: the rule that assets are recorded at the original amount paid for them

impersonal account.definition: an account that does not relate to a person, but to assets, liabilities, expenses, or income.

income.definition: money received by a person or business

income statement.definition: a financial statement that shows the profit or loss of a business for a period.

insurance.definition: payment made for protection against possible loss or damage.

interest.definition: money paid for using borrowed money or earned from lending money

inventory.definition: goods a business keeps for sale or for use in providing services

investing activities.definition: business activities involving buying or selling long-term assets or investments.

investment.definition: using money in a business or asset with the hope of gaining benefit later

investor.definition: a person or organisation that puts money into a business to earn profit

invoice.definition: a document showing details and cost of goods sold or bought.

journal.definition: a book or record where business transactions are first written down in date order

journal entry.definition: a record of a business transaction showing which accounts are debited and credited.

journal proper.definition: the main journal used to record transactions that are not entered in special journals.

journal voucher.definition: a source document used to authorise and give evidence for transactions that are not recorded using other source documents

ledger.definition: a book or record that keeps accounts in an organised way.

liabilities.definition: amounts a business owes to other people or organisations.

liability.definition: money that a business owes to other people or businesses.

liquidity.definition: the ability of a business to pay its short-term debts quickly.

loan.definition: money borrowed from a person or institution that must be paid back later

loss.definition: the amount by which expenses are more than income.

machinery.definition: machines used in a business to do work

maintain.definition: to keep something in good order or continue using it properly

matching principle.definition: the rule that expenses should be recorded in the same period as the revenue they helped to earn

materiality principle.definition: the rule that important financial information that can affect decisions should be shown clearly in reports

materials.definition: items or substances used to make or produce something

medieval.definition: related to the period of history called the Middle Ages

monetary unit principle.definition: the rule that business records should be kept using money as the common measure

motor vehicle.definition: a vehicle used by the business for transport.

narrative.definition: a short explanation written in the journal to describe a transaction.

net income.definition: the profit left after expenses are subtracted from revenue

net loss.definition: the amount by which expenses are more than revenue

net purchases.definition: purchases left after subtracting purchases returns from total purchases.

net sales.definition: sales left after subtracting sales returns from total sales.

nominal account.definition: an account for expenses, losses, revenues, or gains that is closed at the end of the period.

non-current asset.definition: an asset that a business uses for more than one year and does not expect to turn into cash soon

non-current liability.definition: a debt that will be paid after more than one year

non-productive assets.definition: assets in a business that are not being fully used to earn revenue

normal balance.definition: the usual side, debit or credit, where an account is expected to have its balance.

objective.definition: something a person or business plans to achieve

occupation.definition: a person’s main job or business used to earn a living

omission.definition: an error caused by leaving out a transaction or entry.

opening entries.definition: the first journal entries made when starting a business or beginning a new accounting period.

opening inventory.definition: the stock of goods a business has at the beginning of an accounting period.

operating activities.definition: day-to-day business actions that bring in or use cash.

outstanding balance.definition: the amount of money that still remains unpaid.

overdraft.definition: money withdrawn from a bank account beyond the amount available, creating a debt to the bank

owner’s equity.definition: the value of the owner’s interest in the business

payable.definition: money that a business must pay to another person or business

payables.definition: amounts a business must pay to suppliers or other people.

payee.definition: the person or business that receives money from a cheque.

payment.definition: money given to buy something or settle an amount owed.

payment voucher.definition: a document used as proof that money has been paid.

personal account.definition: an account that records transactions relating to a person or organisation.

petty cash.definition: a small amount of cash kept for minor daily expenses.

petty cash voucher.definition: a document used as proof for a small payment made from petty cash.

portfolio.definition: a collection of a student’s work kept as evidence of learning

posting.definition: the act of transferring figures from journals to ledger accounts.

premises.definition: the building or place where a business operates.

private ledger.definition: a ledger that keeps confidential business information for limited people to see.

profit.definition: the amount by which income is more than expenses.

profitability.definition: the ability of a business to make profit.

prudence.definition: the practice of being careful in accounting so that assets and income are not overstated

purchase daybook.definition: a book used to record goods bought on credit from suppliers.

purchase returns daybook.definition: a book of prime entry used to record goods that a business returns to suppliers on credit.

purchase returns journal.definition: a book used to record goods returned to suppliers after being bought on credit.

purchases.definition: goods or items bought by a business.

purchases account.definition: an account that records the total value of goods bought by a business.

purchases daybook.definition: a special journal used to record goods bought on credit

purchases journal.definition: a book used to record goods bought on credit from suppliers.

purchases ledger.definition: a subsidiary ledger that keeps accounts of suppliers or creditors.

purchases return.definition: goods that a business sends back to the supplier after buying them.

purchases returns.definition: goods bought by a business but later returned to the supplier.

purchases returns account.definition: an account that records the total value of goods returned to suppliers.

purchases returns daybook.definition: a special journal used to record goods returned by a business to its supplier

purchases returns journal.definition: a book used to record goods returned to suppliers after credit purchases.

real account.definition: an account for assets or liabilities whose balance is carried forward to the next period.

receipt.definition: money received by a business, or a document showing that money has been received.

receivable.definition: money that other people or businesses owe to the business

receivables.definition: amounts owed to a business by customers.

reconciliation.definition: the process of comparing records to make sure figures agree and are correct.

record.definition: to write down information so it can be kept and used later

record-keeping.definition: the process of writing down and storing business records properly.

rent.definition: money paid or received for the use of property or space.

rent income.definition: money received from renting out property or space.

reporting.definition: the act of giving organised information, usually in written form

retained earnings.definition: profit kept in the business instead of being taken out by the owner

returns.definition: goods sent back after being bought or sold.

revenue.definition: money a business earns from selling goods or services

revenue recognition principle.definition: the rule that revenue should be recorded when it is earned, not just when cash is received

risk.definition: the chance that actual results may be different from what was expected, often with possible loss or danger.

salaries.definition: regular payments made to employees, usually monthly.

sale.definition: the exchange of goods or services for money

sales.definition: goods or services sold by a business for money.

sales account.definition: an account that records the total value of goods sold.

sales daybook.definition: a special journal used to record goods sold on credit

sales journal.definition: a book used to record goods sold on credit.

sales ledger.definition: a subsidiary ledger that keeps accounts of customers who buy on credit.

sales return daybook.definition: a book of prime entry used to record goods returned by customers who bought on credit.

sales returns.definition: goods that customers send back to the business after buying them.

sales returns account.definition: an account that records the total value of goods returned by customers.

sales returns daybook.definition: a special journal used to record goods returned by customers

sales returns journal.definition: a book used to record goods returned by customers after credit sales.

service.definition: work done for someone instead of selling a physical product

services.definition: activities or work sold to others that are not physical goods

single entry.definition: a simple book-keeping method where each transaction is recorded once

single entry system.definition: a simple book-keeping system where each transaction is recorded only once, mainly for cash received or paid

sole proprietor.definition: one person who owns and runs a business alone

sole-proprietor.definition: the single owner of a business

solvency.definition: the ability of a business to pay its long-term debts.

source document.definition: an original document that provides proof that a business transaction took place

stakeholder.definition: a person or group with an interest in the business, such as owners, creditors, or managers.

stakeholders.definition: people or groups who have an interest in a business, such as owners, customers, banks, and suppliers.

statement.definition: a written report showing financial information

statement of account.definition: a document showing amounts billed, amounts paid, and the balance still owed.

statement of affairs.definition: a statement that lists assets and liabilities on a certain date to help find capital

statement of financial position.definition: a financial statement that shows the assets, liabilities, and capital of a business at a certain date.

stock.definition: goods kept by a business for sale or use

stock turnover.definition: a measure of how many times inventory is sold and replaced during a period.

subsidiary ledger.definition: a ledger that contains separate accounts for individual customers or suppliers.

supplier.definition: a person or business that provides goods to another business.

system.definition: an organised way of doing things

tax.definition: money paid to the government by individuals or businesses.

time period principle.definition: the rule that business activities should be reported over set periods such as months or years

trade payables.definition: money a business owes to suppliers for goods bought on credit.

trade receivables.definition: money owed to a business by customers who bought goods on credit.

transaction.definition: a business activity that is recorded, such as buying, selling, or returning goods.

transparency.definition: the quality of being open and clear so others can understand what is happening

transposition error.definition: a mistake made by reversing the order of digits, such as writing 54 instead of 45.

trial balance.definition: a list of all ledger balances prepared to check that total debits equal total credits.

utilisation.definition: the way something is used, especially how well assets are used in a business.

wages.definition: money paid to workers for the work they do.
